resources.string: No device has asked your router to open a port.
Your router does not say which ports are open. Routers only answer when UPnP is on in their settings, and off is the safer choice.
Websites and services see this address when anyone in your home uses them.
Your DeKoi reports this with its next hourly check.
DeKoi sees only its own traffic, so it cannot show how much each device uses. A mode that can is planned.
Once a night your DeKoi downloads 25 MB from Cloudflare and measures how fast it arrives. It counts towards your data allowance, if you have one.
Turn it on to see how fast your connection is.
The first result arrives after the next night.
Some web addresses lead to the wrong place

Your DeKoi looked up well-known web addresses through your router and through an independent service. Twice in a row the answers were different. Someone may have changed your router’s settings to send you to other websites.

Open your router’s app or web page and look at its DNS settings. If you did not set them, set them back to automatic, change the router’s password and update its software. Until then, avoid signing in to important accounts on this network.
A device can now be reached from the internet
A device on your network asked your router to open a port to the internet, and the router did. Games consoles, cameras and file sharing apps do this so that others can connect to them.
If you expected this, there is nothing to do. If not, find the device under Network insights and turn off UPnP in your router’s settings. The router then closes ports opened this way.
